title: Zechariah 10:1–12
context: The prophet calls the people to ask the LORD for rain rather than trust teraphim and diviners. Because they wander “like sheep” with “no shepherd”, the LORD’s anger burns against the false shepherds, and he promises to strengthen Judah, save the house of Joseph, and gather the scattered from Egypt and Assyria. In verses 3–12 the LORD speaks in the first person, with references to the LORD in the third person mixed in, which is common in prophetic speech. Shared ground: the LORD is the true provider and shepherd of his people, and both traditions read the regathering through historic, symbolic, and future lenses.

verses.text: Ask of the LORD rain in the spring time, the LORD who makes storm clouds, and he gives rain showers to everyone for the plants in the field.
verses.arminianNotes: “Ask of the LORD rain in the spring time”. Arminian readers see a call to depend on God for daily provision, a real invitation to pray and receive. The LORD “gives rain showers to everyone”, showing generous care.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same call to prayer, with God as the one who sovereignly sends rain. Shared ground: God commands his people to ask, and he is the one “who makes storm clouds,” not the false sources named in the next verse.

verses.text: For the teraphim have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie; and they have told false dreams. They comfort in vain. Therefore they go their way like sheep. They are oppressed, because there is no shepherd.
verses.arminianNotes: “For the teraphim have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie”. Arminian readers see the people choosing false guidance and suffering for it: they go their way like sheep, oppressed “because there is no shepherd”, language the Gospels echo in Matthew 9:36.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same failure of leadership and stress the people’s need for a true shepherd whom God provides. Shared ground: false comfort leaves people scattered and oppressed, and only the LORD’s guidance is trustworthy.

verses.text: My anger is kindled against the shepherds, and I will punish the male goats, for the LORD of Armies has visited his flock, the house of Judah, and will make them as his majestic horse in the battle.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD says, “My anger is kindled against the shepherds,” and he will punish the male goats. Arminian readers see leaders held responsible for misleading the flock, while the LORD himself visits Judah and makes them like a war horse.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same judgment on unfaithful leaders and God’s gracious transformation of a scattered flock into a strong force. Shared ground: God cares for his flock and holds its shepherds accountable.

verses.text: From him will come the cornerstone, from him the tent peg, from him the battle bow, from him every ruler together.
verses.arminianNotes: “From him will come the cornerstone, from him the tent peg”. Interpreters debate whether “him” is Judah or the LORD. Arminian readers note that many Christian readers have heard messianic overtones in the cornerstone, while others read the images as stable leaders from Judah.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers also note both readings and often connect the cornerstone with Christ, without making the verse carry more than it states. Shared ground: God will raise up stable and faithful leadership for his people, and 2 Samuel 7 stands behind the hope for a ruler from Judah.

verses.text: They will be as mighty men, treading down muddy streets in the battle. They will fight, because the LORD is with them. The riders on horses will be confounded.
verses.arminianNotes: “They will fight, because the LORD is with them.” Arminian readers see God’s presence as the source of their strength, with the people actively engaged rather than passive, treading down enemies like mud in the streets.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same truth: victory comes because the LORD is with them. Shared ground: the riders on horses are confounded not by superior numbers but by the presence of the LORD with his people.

verses.text: “I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back, for I have mercy on them. They will be as though I had not cast them off, for I am the LORD their God, and I will hear them.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD promises, “I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph.” Arminian readers see mercy freely given to a people who had been cast off, with the LORD promising, “I will hear them”, which implies a renewed relationship of prayer and response.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same mercy as rooted in God’s covenant faithfulness: “for I am the LORD their God”. Shared ground: north and south are both restored, and they will be “as though I had not cast them off,” a striking picture of full forgiveness.

verses.text: Ephraim will be like a mighty man, and their heart will rejoice as through wine. Yes, their children will see it and rejoice. Their heart will be glad in the LORD.
verses.arminianNotes: “Ephraim will be like a mighty man”. Arminian readers see joy spreading through the generations, as children see God’s work and rejoice. The northern tribes, long scattered, are pictured restored to strength.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same joy and stress that its source is the LORD: “Their heart will be glad in the LORD.” Shared ground: restoration produces gladness, not only victory, and it reaches the next generation.

verses.text: I will signal for them and gather them, for I have redeemed them. They will increase as they were before.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD says, “I will signal for them and gather them, for I have redeemed them.” Arminian readers see the gathering resting on a redemption already accomplished, which the people are called to answer.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same order: God redeems, then gathers. Shared ground: the LORD whistles for his scattered people like a shepherd, and they will increase as they were before.

verses.text: I will sow them among the peoples. They will remember me in far countries. They will live with their children and will return.
verses.arminianNotes: “I will sow them among the peoples.” Arminian readers note that the scattering is pictured as sowing seed, with the hope that “They will remember me in far countries” and return, a turning that involves the people’s own memory and response.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same image and stress God’s purpose in scattering as well as gathering. Shared ground: even dispersion serves God’s plan, and his people remember him and return with their children.

verses.text: I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria. I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and there won’t be room enough for them.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD will bring them back from Egypt and Assyria into Gilead and Lebanon, until “there won’t be room enough for them.” Arminian readers see the old enemies of Israel named as places from which God will gather his people, a sign that no exile is too far for him.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same promise and note that readers in both traditions differ on whether it was fulfilled in returns after the exile, is fulfilled spiritually in the church, or awaits a future regathering. Shared ground: the LORD’s promise of restoration is abundant and sure.

verses.text: He will pass through the sea of affliction, and will strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up; and the pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart.
verses.arminianNotes: “He will pass through the sea of affliction, and will strike the waves in the sea,” language that recalls the exodus. Arminian readers see God repeating his great act of deliverance, bringing down Assyria’s pride and Egypt’s scepter.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same new exodus and stress God’s power over the nations that once enslaved and scattered his people. Shared ground: the God who split the sea will do it again, and the proud powers of the world will fall before him.

verses.text: I will strengthen them in the LORD. They will walk up and down in his name,” says the LORD.
verses.arminianNotes: “I will strengthen them in the LORD. They will walk up and down in his name,” says the LORD. Arminian readers see a restored people living out their faith actively, walking in the LORD’s name as the evidence of renewed relationship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same strengthening as God’s work in his people, enabling them to walk in his ways. Shared ground: the chapter ends with God’s people secure and faithful, their strength and their walk grounded in the LORD.
